negative_findings.description: No publicly accessible Hungarian-market Visa or Mastercard rulebook, bulletin, or mandatory-deadline register was found. Searches in Hungarian ('szabálykönyv', 'kötelező határidő', 'bankkártya elfogadás') returned only consumer marketing, FAQ and media pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Card scheme rulebooks and Announcement/Bulletin releases appear to be member-only (licensed) documents with no HU-specific public portal identified in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A whole mandatory-deadline stream (scheme release cycles, mandates on issuers/acquirers) is invisible from open sources; the workstream must rely on proxies (acquirer merchant manuals, PSP release notes, trade press) or licensed access.

negative_findings.description: GIRO's participant-facing portal online.giro.hu/dokumentumtar was surfaced by search but its public accessibility was not established in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as a hypothesis: likely partially or fully gated behind a participant login. Not confirmed dead or blocked.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If gated, the richest technical change-notice channel is unavailable, and monitoring must fall back to the public giro.hu/dokumentumok mirror with a lag.

negative_findings.description: No RSS/Atom or structured change-log feed was identified for GIRO Zrt. rulebook amendments; changes appear to be signalled only by new dated PDF filenames.
negative_findings.result_summary: Detection will require filename/hash diffing rather than feed subscription.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Increases collection cost and raises the risk of missing a short-notice effective date.

negative_findings.description: No public, versioned 'qvik szabálykönyv' (qvik scheme rulebook) document with an explicit version number and change history was located; MNB publishes FAQ pages, an arculati kézikönyv and a technikai kézikönyv instead.
negative_findings.result_summary: The qvik scheme obligation set appears distributed across MNB recommendations, technical/brand manuals and the BKR ÜSZ annexes rather than a single rulebook.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Deadline extraction for qvik must aggregate several document families; a single-document monitor would under-cover.

coverage_gaps.description: Card scheme layer (Visa CEMEA, Mastercard Europe) has no identified authoritative HU-facing source; only proxies and media.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Evaluate licensed access (Visa Online / Mastercard Connect via a partner institution) or systematically collect HU acquirer and PSP merchant manuals and release notes as proxies.

coverage_gaps.description: Domestic ATM/card processing and switching operators (e.g. processors serving HU banks) and the BÉT (Budapest Stock Exchange) trading-side rulebooks were not explored in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up sweep on 'kártyaelfogadói hálózat üzemeltető', 'ATM üzemeltető', 'BÉT szabályzat módosítás' to complete the infrastructure actor map.

coverage_gaps.description: Most confirmed effective dates found are 2024-2025; no 2026 forward calendar of Hungarian scheme deadlines was assembled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a deadline register by extracting hatálybalépés dates from KELER Hírcenter, giro.hu dated PDFs and MNB qvik pages, and reconcile against the EU IPR/VoP milestone calendar.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of Hungarian scheme rulebooks is thin — GIRO publishes some EN business terms but Hungarian is the authoritative version.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat Hungarian documents as primary and budget for HU-language parsing/translation; do not rely on EN mirrors for deadline extraction.

brief: Hungary's payments infrastructure obligation stream is concentrated in three operator families: GIRO Zrt. (BKR batch clearing plus GIROInstant/AFR, with GIROLock PKI and GIROHáló network as mandatory access services), the MNB acting as de facto qvik scheme owner and approver of GIRO's business rules, and the KELER / KELER KSZF pair on the securities settlement and CCP side. All three publish binding documents with explicit Hungarian-language effective dates ('hatálybalépés'), but the signalling mechanics differ sharply: KELER runs an explicit Hírcenter announcement feed naming each leirat and its effective date, while GIRO signals changes mainly through newly dated PDF filenames in its public document repository with no change feed, and MNB mirrors approved BKR annexes under mnb.hu/letoltes. The weakest cell coverage is the card scheme layer — Visa and Mastercard rulebooks and mandate bulletins are member-confidential, so open-source tracking must rely on proxies such as Hungarian acquirer merchant acceptance manuals, PSP release notes and trade outlets like FinTechZone, which in practice report Hungarian rulebook changes faster and more concretely than the operators themselves. Upstream, EPC rulebook versions and the EU Instant Payments Regulation / Verification of Payee milestones set the calendar that Hungarian scheme changes are increasingly pegged to.
